title: The Billionaire Who Drove a 1993 Volvo
hook_text: HE FLEW ECONOMY WHILE SITTING ON BILLIONS

beats.say: He flew coach, drove a beat-up Volvo, and reused his tea bags to save pennies.
beats.visual: A minimalist airplane seat in dim cabin lighting, viewed from behind an empty tray table.

beats.say: This billionaire wasn't cheap. He used frugality as a lethal weapon to build a retail empire.
beats.visual: A dark, empty parking lot with a single old station wagon under a flickering streetlamp.

beats.say: Meet Ingvar Kamprad. In 1976, he wrote a manifesto called 'The Testament of a Furniture Dealer'.
beats.visual: Close-up of old weathered paper pages on a dark wooden desk, moody side lighting.

beats.say: His core belief was simple: wastefulness is a deadly sin.
beats.visual: Hands folding a simple blank sheet of paper neatly on a minimal wooden table.

beats.say: Kamprad bought clothes at flea markets. He insisted his executives write on both sides of every paper.
beats.visual: A fountain pen writing on the blank back side of a used piece of paper.

beats.say: But here's the part nobody mentions. This wasn't about suffering.
beats.visual: A close-up of a hand turning off a bright modern desk lamp, leaving soft ambient light.

beats.say: It was a system. Every dollar he didn't waste on luxury went straight back into cutting prices.
beats.visual: A factory floor in warm shadow, showing rows of raw timber stacked neatly.

beats.say: Lower prices meant more customers. More customers meant massive buying power.
beats.visual: An abstract, perfectly organized warehouse shelf system shot from a high angle.

beats.say: He turned personal stinginess into a massive competitive advantage that crushed every rival in sight.
beats.visual: A silhouette of a person walking down a long, dimly lit minimalist hallway.

beats.say: True wealth isn't about what you spend to impress people.
beats.visual: A clean, empty wooden table with a single cup of black coffee casting a long shadow.

beats.say: It's about keeping what you earn and letting it compound. Follow for the money rules
beats.visual: A close-up of hands typing numbers into a vintage calculator on a dark desk.
